items.title: spec: configurable word delimiters for word-deletion shortcuts (#10348)

labels.name: external-contributor
labels.description: Indicates that a PR has been opened by someone outside the Warp team.

items.body:
## Summary

Spec for #10348. Makes the set of characters that act as word boundaries configurable for **all four** word-cursor shortcuts: Delete Word Left, Delete Word Right, Move Cursor Word Left, Move Cursor Word Right. Today these shortcuts treat path-like strings (e.g. `/var/www/example.com/logs`) as a single word; with a configurable delimiter set including `/`, `.`, `-`, `_`, `:`, `=`, the shortcuts split per segment, matching VS Code, JetBrains, and Sublime conventions.

## What's specified

- New `editor.word_delimiters` setting (string of literal characters) with a sensible default: `"/.-_:= \t\n\r\x0b\x0c"`.
- Per-input-context overrides: `terminal.word_delimiters`, `agent.word_delimiters` (both fall back to `editor.word_delimiters`, then to the built-in default).
- Whitespace is **always** a delimiter regardless of configuration (B5) — prevents broken configs.
- Delimiter run collapse semantics matching modern editors (B7).
- Acceptance criteria (A1–A9), test plan (T1–T10), implementation pointers, and a V1.5 deferral for regex-based boundaries.

This spec affects 4 shortcuts (Delete Word Left/Right, Move Cursor Word Left/Right) so they share one boundary definition rather than diverging.

## Test plan

Spec-only PR. Tests T1–T10 will be implemented alongside the code change.

- [ ] T1: default behavior on path string
- [ ] T2: custom delimiter set
- [ ] T3: context override precedence
- [ ] T4: empty setting fallback
- [ ] T5: whitespace forced as delimiter
- [ ] T6: delimiter run collapse on `foo//bar`
- [ ] T7: word-navigation parity with deletion
- [ ] T8: live effect without restart
- [ ] T9: setting persists across restart
- [ ] T10: UTF-8 multi-byte safety

/label ready-to-spec

items.title: Add change-keybinding bundled skill for Agent Mode

labels.name: external-contributor
labels.description: Indicates that a PR has been opened by someone outside the Warp team.

items.body:
## Description

Adds a new bundled skill at \`resources/bundled/skills/change-keybinding/\` that teaches Warp's Agent Mode how to remap keyboard shortcuts when the user asks (e.g. _"Please change ctrl+space mapping to ctrl+s"_).

The skill walks the agent through:
- Discovering the right \`~/.warp*/keybindings.yaml\` file (channel-aware via \`ls -d ~/.warp*/\`).
- The YAML format, including the **mandatory quoting** of action names that contain \`:\`.
- Keystroke encoding: modifier order, the **uppercase-after-shift** rule, special key names, multi-keystroke chords (space-separated), and the \`none\` removal sentinel.
- The discoverability gap — defaults are compiled into Rust and not introspectable from disk, so the agent must \`ask_user_question\` rather than guess when it can't find the binding in the user's yaml.
- The fact that \`keybindings.yaml\` is read only at app launch (via \`load_custom_keybindings\` in \`app/src/lib.rs\`), so the user must restart Warp.

No Rust changes are needed: \`SkillManager::load_bundled_skills\` (\`app/src/ai/skills/skill_manager.rs:421\`) auto-discovers any directory under \`resources/bundled/skills/\` with a \`SKILL.md\`, and the default \`BundledSkillActivation::Always\` is appropriate since this skill doesn't depend on a bundled resource file.

## Testing

Tested manually in a local \`./script/run\` build of the OSS channel against \`~/.warp-oss/keybindings.yaml\`:
- _"Please change ctrl+space mapping to ctrl+s"_ → agent grepped the yaml, didn't find a match (default), and used \`ask_user_question\` to disambiguate the action instead of guessing. ✓
- Direct rebinds by action name produced correctly-quoted entries with the right keystroke normalization (including \`shift-A\` casing). ✓
- Multi-keystroke chords (\`cmd-shift-D escape\`) produced as expected. ✓
- Removal via \`none\` sentinel applied correctly. ✓
- After restarting Warp, the new bindings took effect, confirming the format the skill produces is one Warp's parser actually accepts.

No automated test added — the skill is a markdown content file with no executable surface beyond what the existing \`read_bundled_skills\` parser already covers, and behavior is LLM-driven.

## Server API dependencies

N/A — no server changes.

## Agent Mode
- [ ] Warp Agent Mode - This PR was created via Warp's AI Agent Mode

## Changelog Entries for Stable

CHANGELOG-IMPROVEMENT: Agent Mode can now help you remap Warp keyboard shortcuts — ask it to change a shortcut and it will edit your keybindings.yaml for you.

Co-Authored-By: Warp <agent@warp.dev>

items.title: Fix macOS editing shortcuts dropped in non-KKP alt-screen TUIs
items.body:
## Description
macOS line-editing shortcuts (`cmd-left`, `cmd-right`, `cmd-backspace`, `cmd-delete`, `alt-left`, `alt-right`, `alt-backspace`) were silently dropped inside non-KKP alt-screen TUIs (e.g. `fzf`, `less`) because seven bindings in `app/src/terminal/view/init.rs` were gated on `id!("LongRunningCommand")` alone. `TerminalView::keymap_context` explicitly suppresses `LongRunningCommand` while the alt screen is active, so the predicate could never match.

Other bindings in the same file (e.g. `backward_tabulation` for shift-tab) already use `id!("LongRunningCommand") | id!("AltScreen")`. This PR applies the same widening to the seven editing bindings (word left/right, home/end, delete word left, delete to line start/end).

The underlying action handler (`control_sequence_on_terminal`) already gates on the block's actual long-running state independent of the keymap context flag, so no other logic changes were required.

### Kitty keyboard protocol carve-out
Widening on `AltScreen` alone would have regressed #14012. `AltScreenElement::dispatch_event` only falls back to the KKP-aware encoder (`KeystrokeWithDetails::to_escape_sequence`) when *no* keybinding claimed the keystroke, so an unconditional `AltScreen` match would hijack these chords inside KKP-negotiating TUIs (Claude Code, opencode, …) and replace `CSI 1;3D` / `CSI 127;3u` with legacy control characters.

The seven predicates are therefore consolidated into a single shared `executing_command_editing_context()` helper — so they cannot drift from one another — with the KKP exclusion applied to the alt-screen arm:

```rust
id!("Terminal")
    & !id!("IMEOpen")
    & (id!("LongRunningCommand") | (id!("AltScreen") & !id!(KEYBOARD_PROTOCOL_ENABLED_KEY)))
```

**What this deliberately does not change:** the `LongRunningCommand` arm is left untouched. The sibling `shift-enter` binding applies `!id!(KEYBOARD_PROTOCOL_ENABLED_KEY)` to its whole predicate; doing the same here would also change today's normal-screen behavior for KKP sessions with a running command, which nobody reported, is outside the scope of #14835, and is not covered by any test in this PR. Flagging it explicitly in case a reviewer would prefer that broader change as a follow-up.

Note the widening applies on Linux/Windows too (`ctrl-left` / `ctrl-right` / `ctrl-backspace`), since these are the same binding entries with per-platform keystrokes. That makes alt-screen behavior consistent with the normal-screen behavior those platforms already have.

## Linked Issue
- [x] The linked issue is `factory-auto-implement`.
- [x] No UI changes; screenshots/video not applicable.

Fixes #14835

## Testing
Two regression tests in `app/src/terminal/view_tests.rs`, both simulating a long-running block that swaps to the alt screen:
- `alt_screen_editing_shortcuts_are_dispatched_without_kkp` — no KKP negotiated: asserts the keymap context has `AltScreen` but not `LongRunningCommand`, the keystroke is handled, and `ESC b` reaches the PTY. Fails without the `AltScreen` widening.
- `alt_screen_editing_shortcuts_are_not_dispatched_with_kkp` — KKP negotiated after the screen swap: asserts the keymap context has both `AltScreen` and `KeyboardProtocolEnabled`, the keystroke is **not** claimed by a binding, and no legacy control sequence is written, i.e. it falls through to the #14012 encoder. Verified this test fails (`handled == true`) when the `!id!(KEYBOARD_PROTOCOL_ENABLED_KEY)` exclusion is removed, and passes with it.

Commands run in this sandbox (Linux), all against the current branch head:
- `cargo test -p warp --lib alt_screen_editing_shortcuts` — **2 passed, 0 failed.**
- `cargo test -p warp --lib terminal::view::tests` — 149 passed, 5 failed. The 5 failures (`test_insert`, `test_insert_into_input`, `test_reinput_blocks`, `test_viewport_iter_most_recent_at_bottom`, `test_scroll_position_doesnt_change_when_block_finished`) are pre-existing parallel-execution flakes: each passes when run individually with `--exact --test-threads=1`, and the Review agent independently reproduced the identical failures on unmodified `master`.
- `./script/format --check` — clean.
- `./script/check_no_inline_test_modules` — clean.
- `cargo clippy -p warp --lib --tests --no-deps -- -D warnings` — exit 0, no warnings.

Not run in this sandbox, and therefore not verified here:
- The full workspace suite / `./script/presubmit` (`cargo nextest` is not installed, and a full-workspace build exceeds this environment's memory limit — the `warp` lib target had to be built with `-j 1` and debuginfo disabled to avoid an OOM kill). CI should cover it.
- Manual verification against a real `fzf` / `less` / Claude Code session on macOS: this is a headless Linux sandbox with no macOS host and no GUI, so the behavior is covered by the unit tests above rather than by hand.

- [ ] I have manually tested my changes locally with `./script/run` (not available in this sandboxed environment; verified via unit tests instead)
